# pmon_user (Data Source)

One principal and the groups it belongs to.

Cheaper than `pmon_users` for checking one person, and it puts one principal in state rather than the whole directory.

pmon provisions a principal from the IdP on first login, so a colleague who has never signed in is not here yet and this fails rather than silently resolving to nothing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pmon_user" "alice" {
  principal = "alice@example.com"
}

output "alice_is_admin" {
  value = contains(data.pmon_user.alice.group_names, "system:admin")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `principal` (String) Principal as pmon knows it, usually an email address.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the principal may authenticate.
- `created_at` (String) When pmon first saw the principal.
- `email` (String) Email address.
- `group_names` (List of String) Groups the principal belongs to, sorted.
- `id` (Number) pmon's internal id.
- `source` (String) `OIDC` for a principal provisioned at login, `LOCAL` otherwise.
